title: EmberHealth POC Infosec Evidence Dossier
content:
Purpose and scope:
This dossier collates the security and compliance artifacts we prepared for the EmberHealth POC (Dedicated deployment, healthcare workload). It is an annotated inventory intended for the EmberHealth security review, internal audit trail, and to accelerate the SOC2-like questionnaire responses requested during the Feb 2026 workshop. Scope: Redwood Dedicated POC cluster, VPC peering to customer test VPC, sample PHI-masked dataset, and deployment demo workload (chat, embeddings). Exclusions: EmberHealth production environments, HIPAA Business Associate Agreement (BAA) negotiation documents (handled by legal separately).

Executive summary (one-paragraph):
EmberHealth and Redwood completed a two-week technical POC that demonstrated a private Dedicated deployment inside a customer-controlled VPC with network isolation, customer-managed keys, and RBAC-scoped operator access. The attached artifacts provide evidence for network configuration, key-management integration, access reviews, and runtime logging. Remaining items before a production go/no-go: complete automated key-rotation proof, finalize audit-log retention agreement, and sign the tailored BAA.

Questionnaire highlights (annotated answers):
- Q: Where are customer data and model artifacts stored?
  A: Customer data for the POC was mounted to a customer-managed S3 bucket (arn:aws:s3:::emberhealth-poc-data) accessible only via the VPC endpoint; no data was persisted on shared Redwood buckets. Model artifacts used were a pre-approved open model image pulled to the Dedicated nodes and stored on encrypted EBS volumes (see artifact: node-ebs-encryption.pdf).
- Q: Who has administrative access to the POC cluster?
  A: Admin access is limited to EmberHealth engineers plus a scoped Redwood SE account used for deployment assistance (IAM role: redwood-poc-se-2026). Cross-account assume-role logs are included in audit evidence.
- Q: How is encryption at rest/in transit ensured?
  A: TLS1.2+ enforced for all endpoints; mTLS used for node-to-node RPC inside the cluster. At rest: EBS volumes encrypted with customer-managed CMK; S3 encryption SSE-KMS (customer CMK). Evidence: kms-rotation-policy.pdf, s3-bucket-policy.json, tls-config-snippets.txt.

Evidence inventory (annotated):
- ember-network-architecture.pdf — diagram of VPC peering, subnets, NAT/GW placement, and security groups used for the POC. (Annotated by SE: shows private subnets restricted to EmberHealth CIDR blocks.)
- kms-rotation-policy.pdf — export of the customer-managed KMS key policy and rotation schedule used during POC.
- node-ebs-encryption.pdf — cloud provider console screenshots showing EBS encryption flags and CMK ARNs.
- access-audit-crossaccount.log — filtered CloudTrail export showing assume-role events for redwood-poc-se-2026 between 2026-02-12 and 2026-02-24.
- svc-account-list.csv — list of service accounts and their IAM roles used by the Dedicated cluster (redacted UIDs).
- app-logs-trace-sample.json — truncated application traces demonstrating request-level logging and request IDs for replay/eval. Sensitive fields redacted; masking script attached as redaction-script.sh.
- infra-terraform-plan.txt — snapshot of final terraform plan used to instantiate POC infra (sensitive variables removed).
- s3-bucket-policy.json — explicit policy showing bucket ACL, VPC endpoint restriction, and deny for public access.
- tls-config-snippets.txt — snippets of server and client TLS config demonstrating cipher suites and protocol enforcement.
- access-review-se-minutes.docx — minutes from the access review meeting on 2026-02-20, includes sign-off lines from EmberHealth SecOps.

Controls mapping (high-level):
- Network controls: ember-network-architecture.pdf maps to NIST 800-53 SC-7 and SOC2 CC6.
- Encryption controls: kms-rotation-policy.pdf, node-ebs-encryption.pdf map to SOC2 CC6 and ISO27001 A.10.
- Access logs / monitoring: access-audit-crossaccount.log and app-logs-trace-sample.json map to SOC2 CC7 and internal alerting playbooks.

Workshop notes (Feb 18–19, 2026):
- Attendees (Redwood): Aisha Thompson (SE lead), Marco Ruiz (security), Priya Nair (SRE); (EmberHealth): Claire Wong (SecOps), Daniel Park (Platform), Maria Soto (Compliance).
- Runbook walkthrough: we demoed failover path when Dedicated pool loses a node and validated automatic routing to the standby model variant. Action: update runbook to include explicit steps for rotating CMKs in-place (owner: Marco, due 2026-03-12).
- Data-flow exercise: stepped through request lifecycle from EmberHealth client -> VPC endpoint -> model serving node. Identified a minor gap in request-level redaction when logs include free-form user inputs; mitigation: apply redaction lambda on log ingestion (owner: Priya, due 2026-03-08).
- Compliance Q&A: EmberHealth requested evidence of monthly access reviews and a copy of our incident response runbook. We provided the access-review-se-minutes.docx and linked the IR runbook draft (Confluence). IR runbook finalization (owner: Lena, due 2026-03-15).

Risk register (POC-specific):
- Risk: Key rotation not demonstrable end-to-end during POC. Impact: Medium. Mitigation: run an in-situ rotation test on a staging node and capture telemetry; produce rotation proof artifact (owner: Marco).
- Risk: Logs contain unredacted PII in rare edge-case prompts. Impact: High for health data. Mitigation: apply streaming redaction at ingestion and add regex tests in CI (owner: Priya).
- Risk: SLA expectations for Dedicated throughput not finalized. Impact: Medium. Mitigation: produce benchmark report for EmberHealth workload (owner: SE team).

Open action items (summary):
- Produce automated key rotation proof and place artifact in this dossier (owner: Marco Ruiz, due 2026-03-12).
- Implement streaming redaction lambda and add CI unit tests for masking (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-03-08).
- Confirm audit-log retention window with EmberHealth legal and update retention policy document (owner: Aisha Thompson, due 2026-03-10).
- Finalize BAA draft and route to legal for signature (owner: Legal - Ana Patel, due 2026-03-22).

Handover checklist for production readiness (POC -> Private Dedicated):
- Completed evidence artifacts above and acceptance by EmberHealth SecOps.
- BAA executed.
- Benchmark report and agreed throughput SLOs.
- Confirmed CMK rotation SOP and automation.
- Automated redaction in place and tested.
- SRE playbook for incident escalation validated with EmberHealth contacts.

- Redwood Security SMEs: Marco Ruiz — marco@redwood.ai; Lena Ortiz — lena@redwood.ai
- EmberHealth SecOps: Claire Wong — claire.wong@emberhealth.org

Appendix: sample artifact access instructions
- CloudTrail exports: stored in internal secure bucket (link provided to EmberHealth IAM role). Request via SE ticket SEC-4729 for temporary access zip.
- Terraform snapshots: refer to infra-terraform-plan.txt in this folder. For full state access, request signed NDA/approval.

Notes on provenance and redactions:
- All artifacts included in this dossier have been reviewed to remove direct PHI. Where record-level data was required for debugging, we replaced identifiers with stable-redacted tokens and attached the redaction-script.sh that codifies the transformation. Original debug artifacts are available under embargo to EmberHealth audit team under request and DPA.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Deliver key-rotation proof (Marco).
2) Deploy redaction lambda to ingestion pipeline and run end-to-end log redaction test (Priya).
3) Schedule final evidence review with EmberHealth SecOps (Aisha) — proposed week of 2026-03-15.

Document history and revisions:
- 2026-02-10: Initial draft created to capture artifacts collected during POC.
- 2026-02-20: Added access-review minutes and updated evidence inventory.
- 2026-03-05: Incorporated workshop clarifications and listed final open actions (current).

If anything in this dossier appears incomplete or you need full raw copies under embargo, please open JIRA SEC-4729 and assign to Aisha Thompson.
